stem.text: A composite rod is made by attaching a glass-reinforced plastic rod and a nylon rod end to end, as shown.

stem.alt: Horizontal rod made of two cylinders joined end to end, each marked with a length of 1.00 m above it; the left one labelled glass-reinforced plastic with E_p = 40 GPa and the right one labelled nylon with E_n = 2.0 GPa; arrows at both ends of the rod point outwards.

stem.text: The rods have the same cross-sectional area and each rod is $1.00\,\text{m}$ in length. The Young modulus $E_\text{p}$ of the plastic is $40\,\text{GPa}$ and the Young modulus $E_\text{n}$ of the nylon is $2.0\,\text{GPa}$.
The composite rod will break when its total extension reaches $3.0\,\text{mm}$.
What is the greatest tensile stress that can be applied to the composite rod before it breaks?
